description: Umbilical cable, module to instrument
notes: *** GAUGE IS OPEN AND THREE DERIVATIONS ASSUME 24 AWG. *** 0005:91 computes a ~0.34 ohm round trip, breath-sense-link.md:100 a 0.168 ohm return term, and 0003:315 a whole signal-drop table - all at 24 AWG, which this row does not specify. A stranded Cat5e PATCH lead is commonly 26 or 28 AWG, at 1.6x to 2.6x the resistance. WHAT DECIDES IT: buy the lead, read the jacket print, or measure end-to-end DC resistance at E6. part: PEM FHL-M2.5-8ZI self-clinching flush-head stud, low-displacement head, zinc-plated steel
description: Pressed into the key plate at each key-board corner, head flush with the plate's top face; carries the spacer, key board and nut below
notes: ONE PER KEY-BOARD CORNER: count = the sum of drc.echo "key-board mounts" over both boards. PRESSED INTO THE PLATE BY THE PLATE VENDOR (or on a press): hole hardware.kb_stud_hole, NOT DEBURRED, stud inserted from the punch side, squeezed flush on a flat parallel anvil - for sheet this thin, PEM's countersunk anvil 8003302 with punch 975200997 [datasheets/mechanical/PEM-FH-SELF-CLINCHING-STUDS.pdf p.FH-18, FH-20]. Never hammered. FHL, not FH: FHL holds its data in 1.2 mm aluminium and needs 2.8 from an edge, where FH needs 5.4 (hardware.kb_stud_edge; drc.echo "key-board studs clear of the plate's edges and cutouts"); rated for aluminium to HRB 80 / HB 150, so 5052 or 6061 [datasheets/mechanical/PEM-FH-SELF-CLINCHING-STUDS.pdf p.FH-7]. Zinc-plated steel, not stainless: PEM's finish guide calls stainless in aluminium a significant galvanic pair and plated steel acceptable [datasheets/mechanical/PEM-TECHSHEET-CHOOSING-A-FASTENER-FINISH.pdf pp.3-4]. Length: hardware.kb_stud_l; drc.echo "key-board stud: thread past the nut", "key-board stud: its unthreaded shank ends above the board" and "key-board stud ends clear of the main board's parts". TIGHTEN THE NUT TO NO MORE THAN hardware.kb_stud_torque; the clinch holds the stud against turning, so a nut comes off from below with the lid bonded. The board's holes are NPTH and keep copper out round the spacer and nut, except the ONE mount that grounds the plate (key-board-lh layout.yaml bond_mount; ADR 0020 Amendment 5), so there is no second bond. US SOURCE: not yet found for FHL-M2.5-8ZI [UNVERIFIED - ask the plate vendor, who presses them]

part: RTV silicone - ALKOXY (alcohol) neutral cure, electronics-safe
description: Plate to oak, matrix diffuser, thumb plate - and the lid gasket
notes: NOT ACETOXY. The common hardware-store type releases acetic acid while curing, inside a sealed cavity holding two dev boards, a carrier, connectors and a pressure sensor. Compliant in shear so the oak's 0.6-0.9mm of cross-grain humidity movement does not fight the aluminium plate; stiff in compression so the plate is still backed under a key press. BEAD IT, DO NOT BUTTER IT - cure needs atmospheric moisture and runs ~2mm/day inwards, so a trapped full-face layer never cures. Keep it off both sensor ports (ADR 0003), and bond the plate only after both key boards are mounted on its studs and soldered (ADR 0020, Amendment 4); the beads may run over the studs' flush heads | 2026-09-21: TWO JOBS NOW. Adhesive on the permanent joints above; GASKET on the lid-to-U joint, which opens on six fasteners (ADR 0009). Same tube. Lay the gasket bead on ONE face, let it skin, then clamp - a fresh bead glues the lid shut, which is the failure this change exists to avoid
